levels.title: The anatomy of Russian mat and the social risk of using it: root families, force, audience and the safe reply

units.title: The root families: how mat is built from a few roots, and how to read a form you have never seen

lessons.title: Four roots, one machine: how Russian mat is built, and how to read a form you have never seen
lessons.explanation:
Russian mat is better defined by its roots than by a list of forbidden words. The Russian Wikipedia article on русский мат (ROOS-keey MAT), 'Russian obscene language', reports Yu. I. Levin's working definition: mat consists of 'relatively complete' speech segments containing at least one obscene root, and the list of roots can be given, though its edges are fuzzy. Levin's core is the three roots every speaker recognises, and a typical list runs from four to seven items. Speakers disagree at the margin, since гондон (gan-DON), 'condom', is heard as mat by some and as ordinary rudeness by others. That is not a flaw in the definition; it is the definition, because mat is what native speakers treat as mat.

The core is the обсценная триада (ap-STSEN-na-ya TREE-a-da), 'obscene triad': хуй (KHUY), 'prick', пизда (peez-DA), 'cunt', and ебать (ye-BAT'), 'to fuck'. What matters for a learner is a structural fact the same article states plainly: modern Russian has no neutral literary synonyms for these three, and the nearest equivalents are medical terms, often of Latin origin. A mat word is therefore not an informal version of a polite word that can be swapped into the same sentence. It occupies a different slot, and the slot is defined by taboo rather than by meaning.

The inventory is wider than the triad. Plucer-Sarno's survey work, summarised in the same article, found thirty-five roots that respondents treated as mat and identified seven that are most often felt as mat: the triad plus блядь (BLYAT'), 'whore', муде and муды (moo-DYE, moo-DY), 'testicles', манда (man-DA), 'female genitals', and елда (yel-DA), 'male genitals'. блядь is the only item there that denotes neither genitals nor copulation, and by survey rank it comes second after ебать, which is why it is the most frequent mat token in speech and so often carries no target at all.

What makes the system learnable is its derivational productivity. The article quotes V. V. Raskin's list of verbs formed from ебать, and it runs to thirty-seven items, among them ебануть, ебаться, ёбнуть, выебать, доебаться, заебать, наебать, объебать, отъебать, поебать, подъебать, разъебать, съебаться and уебать. V. M. Mokienko's conclusion, quoted there, is that the formation uses 'the whole Russian word-formational paradigmatics of the verbal lexicon', and that nouns and adjectives are equally productive. The article adds a scale worth remembering: the first five to seven roots generate several thousand derivatives between them, while all the remaining roots generate only a few hundred. Mat is therefore not a vocabulary list but a small set of roots plus the ordinary machinery of prefix, suffix and ending, which is why a form you have never seen is usually decodable.

Recognition runs in four steps. Find the root, stripping prefixes until a known root appears. Identify the prefix and its spatial or aspectual sense. Identify the suffix class, since -ну- marks a single act, -ат- builds adjectives of possession, -ня builds nouns of mass, and the participle suffixes -т- and -н- mark a resulting state. Then read the ending, which gives gender, number, case, person or tense exactly as it does anywhere else. Only after those four steps ask what the whole form means, because the answer is often idiomatic. The root supplies the taboo; the affixes supply the grammar and most of the sense.

Etymology needs a warning label. The origin of хуй is unknown; the Wikipedia article devoted to the word says so in its first sentence, then reports three proposals: the academic Этимологический словарь славянских языков connects it with хвоя (KHVO-ya), 'pine needles'; the Slavist Gennady Kovalyov reconstructs a common Slavic *XŪ meaning 'offshoot, shoot'; other work links it to a Proto-Indo-European root *skēu-, 'to be sharp'. A fourth proposal, from V. M. Illich-Svitych, derives it from a Nostratic form for 'thorn', and the article notes that most linguists reject the Nostratic theory. The word мат has its own dispute: the usual account derives it from мать (MAT'), 'mother', as a shortening of матерная брань (ma-TYER-na-ya BRAN'), 'mother-swearing', while an older one derives it from a word for 'voice' in кричать благим матом (kree-CHAT bla-GEEM MA-tam), 'to shout at the top of one's voice', which Berneker and Vasmer rejected. Name the source, name the camp, and never present a contested derivation as settled.

This lesson is descriptive: it teaches what the forms are, how they are built and what they do socially. It does not recommend using any of them against a person, and lesson 137 sets out the audiences in which the risk is real. The ten lessons at ids 21 to 30 already covered the everyday sequence from блин (BLEEN), 'darn', to иди на хуй (ee-DEE na KHUY), 'fuck off'; nothing here repeats them.
lessons.example:
Decode six forms in turn, aloud, using the four steps. First, проебать (pra-ye-BAT'), 'to lose, to screw up'. Strip про-, which marks passage, and the root еб- appears; the theme vowel -а- and the ending -ть mark a first conjugation infinitive. The literal composition is 'to fuck through' and the attested sense is 'to lose or waste', so the form is idiomatic but transparent. Second, доебаться (da-ye-BAT-sa), 'to pester someone'. до- marks arrival at a limit and -ся removes the object, so the verb describes reaching a person with a demand; the reflexive suffix, not the root, creates the sense. Third, хуёвый (khoo-YO-vy), 'crappy'. The root is хуй, the suffix is -ёв-, and -ый marks a soft-stem adjective, predicting хуёвая (khoo-YO-va-ya), хуёвое (khoo-YO-va-ye) and хуёвые (khoo-YO-vy-ye); a learner who knows новый (NO-vy), 'new', already knows the paradigm. Fourth, пиздатый (peez-DA-ty), 'excellent'. The suffix -ат- builds adjectives of possession, as in бородатый (ba-ra-DA-ty), 'bearded', so compositionally the word says 'endowed with' the noun and the positive evaluation is idiomatic drift. Fifth, ёбнутый (YOB-noo-ty), 'unhinged'. The root is in its ё grade, -ну- marks a single blow, and -т- is the participle suffix, so the form means 'one who has been struck', which is the metaphor behind the slang; the feminine is ёбнутая (YOB-noo-ta-ya). Sixth, заёб (za-YOB), 'nuisance': за- marks saturation, the root has a zero suffix, and the noun is masculine inanimate, declining заёба (za-YO-ba) and заёбу (za-YO-boo).

Put the six in a column labelled root, prefix, suffix and grammatical job; that column is the whole method. A learner who meets выёбываться (vy-YO-by-vat-sa), 'to put on airs', runs the same steps: вы- marks emergence, -ыва- repeated action, -ся the absence of an object. Beside each form write the neutral paraphrase you would use yourself. For проебать it is потерять (pa-tee-RYAT'), 'to lose'; for доебаться it is приставать (pree-sta-VAT'), 'to pester'. The paraphrase is your production vocabulary and the mat form is your reading vocabulary, and keeping them apart prevents the commonest adult error, which is using the mat form because it is the only word you have for the idea.
lessons.question: A colleague mutters «Опять доебался до охраны» (a-PYAT' da-ye-BAL-sya da a-KHRA-ny). Applying the four steps, what has he said?
lessons.answer: That someone got on the security guards' case again: до- marks arrival at a target, -ся removes the object, and the verb is idiomatic for pestering someone with complaints.
lessons.distractor: That someone finished having sex with the guards, because до- marks the completion of an action.
lessons.correction: The error is to read the prefix literally and to ignore the reflexive suffix. до- does mark arrival or completion in verbs such as дочитать (da-chee-TAT'), 'to finish reading', so the guess is not random. But with -ся, доебаться means to reach a person with a demand, and the preposition до plus the genitive охраны names the target rather than a partner. The reliable test is the preposition pattern: доебаться до кого-то (da-ye-BAT-sa da ka-VO), 'to pester someone', takes до plus genitive, while the literal verb takes an accusative object. When a prefix plus -ся appears, look for the preposition before you look for a translation.

depth.definitions: Five terms carry the lesson. Mat (MAT) is the Russian name for obscene language, a lexical layer organised around a small set of roots. An obscene root cannot appear in neutral speech at all, so any word containing it inherits the taboo regardless of what the word means. The обсценная триада (ap-STSEN-na-ya TREE-a-da), 'obscene triad', is the triple хуй, пизда and ебать, the anatomical and sexual core of Levin's definition. A derivational family is the set of words built from one root by prefixation and suffixation, and it is the unit this lesson teaches, because the family is what a speaker commands. Desemanticisation is the loss of literal meaning in a fixed expression, so that поебать in мне поебать (mnye pa-YE-bat'), 'I could not care less', no longer refers to sex. Prerequisites are lessons 106 and 107 on verb prefixes and noun suffixes, 108 on adjectives and adverbs from one stem, and 109 on evaluative suffixes.
depth.mechanism:
The root has three shapes. The base is еб-, as in ебать, ебаться and ебальник. Under stress the same root surfaces as ёб-, written with ё in ёбнуть, ёбнутый and заёб, because Russian writes ё only when the vowel is stressed; that is why ебёшь (ye-BYOSH), 'you fuck', has ё while ебу (ye-BOO), 'I fuck', does not. The third shape is the zero grade in ебля (YEB-lya), 'fucking', where no vowel follows the root. None of this is special to mat: it is the alternation that gives несу (nee-SOO), 'I carry', and нёс (NYOS), 'he carried'. Because the root ends in a consonant, every ending attaches without adjustment, which is why the families are so large.

The prefix decides aspect and most of the sense. за- adds saturation, so заебать (za-ye-BAT') is to wear someone out by persistence. вы- adds completion and extraction, so выебать (VY-ye-bat') is to see an act through and, by extension, to chew someone out. на- adds accumulation and, with this root, deception, so наебать (na-ye-BAT') is to cheat. до- adds arrival, so доебаться is to arrive at a person with a complaint. раз- adds dispersal, so разъебать (raz-ye-BAT') is to smash. с- with -ся adds departure, so съебался (s-YE-bal-sya) is 'he fucked off'.

Suffixes fix the part of speech. -ну- marks a single act, so ёбнуть (YOB-noot') is one blow and ёбнутый describes someone who received one. -ёв- builds relational adjectives from nouns, so хуёвый is literally 'of the prick' before it is 'bad'. -ня builds nouns of mass, which is how хуйня (khooy-NYA) means 'junk' as a substance rather than one object. -ёж builds nouns of repeated action, as in пиздёж (peez-DYOSH), 'lying'. -ец appears in пиздец (peez-DYETS) as a terminal-state noun. The participle suffixes -т- and -н- turn a verb into a description of a state, which is why ёбнутый and поёбанный work as adjectives of condition.
depth.secondExample: Two further forms show the method on material not used above. наебать (na-ye-BAT'), 'to cheat, to swindle': на- marks accumulation and perfective sense, the verb is transitive, and the past is наебал (na-ye-BAL) with feminine наебала (na-ye-BA-la). The literal composition, 'to fuck onto someone', is not the meaning, but the prefix plus the transitive frame predicts that someone receives something unwanted, which is enough to guide the reading. ебальник (ye-BAL-neek), 'mug, face': the suffix -льник names instruments and containers, as in умывальник (oo-mee-VAL-neek), 'washbasin', and холодильник (kha-la-DEEL-neek), 'refrigerator', so the noun names the thing the root is associated with. In an invented exchange, parsed: «Он меня наебал на тысячу.» (on mee-NYA na-ye-BAL na TY-se-choo) 'He cheated me out of a thousand.' The accusative меня is the person cheated, на тысячу names the amount, and the verb is perfective past masculine. «Видел бы ты его ебальник.» (VEE-deel by ty ye-VO ye-BAL-neek) 'You should have seen his face.' The бы marks the unreal and ты is the subject of the conditional. Two forms, two grammatical jobs, one root, every ending doing ordinary work: the taboo is lexical, the grammar is not.
depth.mistake:
The characteristic adult error is to translate the root and ignore the affixes, which produces readings that are grammatically confident and semantically wrong. доебаться becomes a sexual act, проебать becomes a sexual failure, and выебать becomes literal even in its common sense of dressing someone down. The diagnostic is simple: if your reading contains the literal meaning of the root while the sentence is about work, money, transport or an argument, you have probably skipped the prefix.

The second error is over-generation. Because the paradigm is productive, learners assume any combination is attested and produce forms that do not exist. Productivity is a property of the system, not a licence for the speaker; the list of thirty-seven verbs is long and it is still a list. The third error is register inflation, treating a mat form as the natural translation of an English expletive, since English swearing is frequent in registers where Russian mat is not. A learner who translates 'this is bullshit' as хуйня in a meeting has made a social error that no grammatical accuracy repairs.
depth.application: In practice this is a reading skill. When you meet an unfamiliar mat form in a subtitle, a comment thread or overheard speech, write it down with four labels, then add one neutral paraphrase and one register note. A notebook entry for доебаться reads: root еб-, prefix до-, suffix -а- plus -ся, perfective verb, 'to pester someone', very obscene, takes до plus genitive. That entry predicts how the word behaves in a sentence, which ten memorised translations do not. The same discipline applies to etymologies in popular writing: when an article claims that a mat word descends from a Tatar word or a pagan ritual, check whether a dictionary is named, and treat any confident derivation without a named source as contested.
depth.summary: Mat is organised around a handful of roots, with the triad хуй, пизда and ебать at the core and a disputed margin that runs to about seven items in most lists. Each root supports a large derivational family built with ordinary Russian prefixes and suffixes, which is why a new form is usually decodable: find the root, identify the prefix and suffix, read the ending, then check the idiom. The prefix carries most of the sense and the aspect, the suffix fixes the part of speech, and the ending does the grammar. Etymologies are the least reliable part of the subject, so name the source and label the contested cases. The next four lessons take the families in turn: хуй in 132, пизда in 133, ебать in 134 and блядь in 135.

visual.description: A labelled text diagram in two panels. The left panel is a tree: one box at the root labelled 'mat', four branches labelled with the core roots, and under each branch a short column of derived forms tagged with their part of speech. The right panel is a four-rung ladder showing the decoding steps in order. Rendered as text steps, not as an image.
steps: Step 1, draw the trunk. One box at the top reads 'mat: a small set of roots, not a word list'. Under it write the triad in one row, хуй, пизда, ебать, and a fourth branch labelled 'peripheral roots' with блядь, манда, елда and муде inside it. Label the margin 'disputed: гондон and similar items'.

Step 2, hang the хуй branch. Three sub-boxes: the noun хуй with its case forms хуя, хую, хуем; the derived nouns хуйня and хуёвина; the adjective and adverb хуёвый and хуёво. Mark every box 'very obscene'.

Step 3, hang the пизда and ебать branches. Under пизда write пиздатый and пиздато as 'positive slang' and спиздить as 'to steal, perfective'. Under ебать write a prefix column, за-, вы-, на-, до-, про-, with one verb beside each, then a separate sub-box for ёбнутый marked 'participle used as adjective'.

Step 4, build the decoding ladder on the right. Four rungs, bottom to top: 'find the root', 'identify the prefix and its sense', 'identify the suffix class', 'read the ending'. Add one margin note at the top: 'only now decide what it means, and check the idiom'.

Step 5, add the worked example beside the ladder. Write доебаться with a bracket under до- labelled 'arrival at a target', a bracket under еб- labelled 'obscene root', a bracket under -а-ть labelled 'first conjugation infinitive', and -ся labelled 'no object'. Beside it write the paraphrase 'to pester someone, takes до plus genitive'.

lessons.title: The хуй (KHUY, 'prick') family: the noun, the derived nouns, the adjective and the fixed idioms
lessons.explanation:
The noun itself is the easy part and the least useful part. хуй (KHUY) is masculine, and its accusative repeats the nominative as it does for inanimate nouns: хуя (khoo-YA) genitive, хую (khoo-YOO) dative, хуем (khoo-YOM) instrumental, хуе (khoo-YE) prepositional. The literal sense is 'prick, dick', and a learner who stops there will understand almost none of the speech in which the word actually occurs. The Russian Wikipedia article on the word is explicit that the literal sense is only one of its uses. It also works as what the article calls a substitute for almost any animate masculine noun, with хуёвина (khoo-YO-vee-na) doing the same job for inanimate things; in that use the emotional colouring is neutral or weakly marked, while хуйня (khooy-NYA) can carry strong emotion. That distribution is the key to the family: the bare noun is often a placeholder, and the derived forms are where the evaluation lives.

Start with the derived nouns. хуйня is feminine, declines like земля (zeem-LYA), 'earth', and means 'junk, nonsense, crap' in three related senses that the Russian Wiktionary entry separates: any thing at all, an unclear or unspecified thing, and a thing of poor quality. хуёвина names a concrete object whose name the speaker either does not know or does not respect, and it is the inanimate counterpart of the placeholder use. Both are extremely obscene and both are banned from Russian media, which is why they appear in speech and in comment threads far more often than in print.

The adjective carries the evaluation. хуёвый (khoo-YO-vy) means 'bad, crappy, lousy', and it is a soft-stem adjective: хуёвая (khoo-YO-va-ya) feminine, хуёвое (khoo-YO-va-ye) neuter, хуёвые (khoo-YO-vy-ye) plural, with the same endings as синий (SEE-nee), 'dark blue'. The adverb хуёво (khoo-YO-va) is the -о form of the neuter short adjective, so it does double duty: it modifies a verb as a manner adverb, and it stands as a one-word predicate meaning 'things are bad'. The Russian Wiktionary entry gives 'very bad, poorly' as the sense and lists хреново (khrye-NO-va) and херово (khye-RO-va) as synonyms, which places the whole set on the euphemism ladder that lesson 138 maps.

The idioms are the real content of the family, and each one has its own grammar. ни хуя (nee khoo-YA) is the genitive of negation: ни requires the genitive, so 'not a fucking thing' is literally 'not of a prick'. It negates a verb emphatically, as in ни хуя не понял (nee khoo-YA ne PO-nyal), 'I did not understand a fucking thing', and in the colloquial spelling нихуя (nee-khoo-YA) it works as a standalone adverb meaning 'not at all'. на хуй (na KHUY) is a directional phrase with на plus the accusative, used to send someone or something away, and it is the obscene core of иди на хуй (ee-DEE na KHUY), 'fuck off'. до хуя (da khoo-YA) uses до plus the genitive for quantity and means 'a hell of a lot'. хуй с ним (KHUY s NEEM) is 'to hell with it', with с plus the instrumental, and it dismisses a thing rather than a person. забить хуй на (za-BEET' KHUY na), literally 'to hammer a prick onto', means to stop caring about something, and it takes на plus the accusative. ни хуя себе (nee khoo-YA see-BYÉ) is an exclamation of surprise, the obscene equivalent of 'well I never'.

Two facts about scale belong here. The Russian Wikipedia article reports Plucer-Sarno's count of more than 1200 clichés built on this root, and 503 idioms and set phrases in the first volume of his dictionary, which makes хуй the most productive root in Russian mat. The same productivity is why the root is one of the four that Roskomnadzor's media guidance names: the ban covers the obscene names of the male organ, the female organ, copulation and a woman of loose behaviour, together with all their derivatives. A learner reading a newspaper will therefore meet the euphemisms from lesson 138 instead, while a learner listening to a conversation will meet the forms above.

One warning belongs in the explanation rather than in the mistakes section, because it is a comprehension issue rather than a production issue. When хуй appears where a person's name should be, the sentence is contemptuous of that person, and the contempt is the point. Learners sometimes read the placeholder use as friendly or as mere filler because the article calls its colouring weak. Weak colouring in a native speaker's mouth is not neutral in a learner's mouth, and lesson 137 explains why the same word can pass between two friends and wound when it comes from someone else.
lessons.example:
Take an invented exchange in a garage and parse every mat form. «Опять эта хуйня не заводится.» (a-PYAT' EH-ta khooy-NYA ne za-VO-deet-sya) 'This piece of crap will not start again.' The demonstrative эта agrees with the feminine хуйня, the verb is reflexive and negated, and the noun is the subject. «Да хуй с ним, поехали на автобусе.» (da KHUY s NEEM, pa-YE-ha-lee na af-TO-boo-sye) 'To hell with it, let us take the bus.' The idiom is fixed, с ним is instrumental, and the main clause is a first person plural imperative in the past tense, which Russian uses for a proposal. «До хуя времени.» (da khoo-YA VRYE-me-nee) 'We have loads of time.' The genitive времени is governed by до, and the phrase is a quantity expression, not a spatial one.

Now the same root in a complaint about a person, where the grammar changes. «Он мне всю неделю мозг выносил, а потом забил хуй.» (on mnye fsyu nee-DYE-lyu mozg VY-na-seel, a pa-TOM za-BEEL KHUY) 'He pestered me all week and then stopped caring altogether.' The second clause has no object for забить beyond the idiom, and the shift from activity to indifference is carried entirely by the fixed phrase. Beside it, the adjectival evaluation: «Хуёвый из него начальник.» (khoo-YO-vy eez nee-VO na-CHAL-neek) 'He is a lousy boss.' The adjective agrees with начальник in the masculine, and the phrase из него plus the nominative is the standard construction for judging someone in a role. Note what has happened across the four sentences: the same root produced a noun of quality, a dismissal idiom, a quantity idiom and an evaluation of a person, and only the last one is aimed at anybody.
lessons.question: A friend says «Хуёво, что ты уезжаешь» (khoo-YO-va, shta ty oo-ye-ZHA-ye-sh). What is the grammar of хуёво here, and what does the sentence mean?
lessons.answer: хуёво is the predicative adverb 'it is bad', the что-clause is its subject, and the sentence means 'it is a shame you are leaving'.
lessons.distractor: хуёво is a manner adverb modifying уезжаешь, so the sentence means 'you are leaving badly'.
lessons.correction: The formal clue is the comma and the word order. A manner adverb sits next to its verb and answers 'how', as in он хуёво работает (on khoo-YO-va ra-BO-ta-yeet), 'he works badly'. Here хуёво stands first, is separated by a comma, and takes a whole clause as its subject, which is the predicative pattern Russian shares with холодно (KHO-lad-na), 'it is cold' and жаль (ZHAL'), 'it is a pity'. The learner's error is to assume that an -о form must modify a verb. In fact the -о form is the neuter short adjective, and short adjectives are predicates by default; the adverbial use is the derived one. Recognising the pattern matters for comprehension, because the two readings differ in who is being evaluated: the manner reading criticises the friend's departure, while the predicative reading expresses regret.

depth.definitions: The family turns on four categories. Animacy is the grammatical feature that decides whether the accusative copies the nominative, and хуй is treated as inanimate, so the accusative is хуй rather than хуя. The genitive of negation is the rule that ни and negated existence take the genitive, which is why ни хуя is genitive and not accusative. A placeholder noun is a noun used where a specific noun is expected, with the referent recoverable from context, and хуй in that use is closer to a pronoun than to a name for a body part. A fixed idiom is a phrase whose meaning cannot be computed from its parts, and the хуй family has more of them than any other mat root, which is the reason the family deserves a lesson rather than a glossary entry. Prerequisites are lesson 51 on the accusative, lesson 53 on the genitive after prepositions, and lesson 108 on adjectives and adverbs from one stem.
depth.mechanism:
Three mechanisms generate the whole family. The first is case government. Prepositions and negators select a case, and the case changes the meaning of the phrase in a predictable way: на plus accusative gives direction, до plus genitive gives extent or quantity, с plus instrumental gives accompaniment, and ни plus genitive gives categorical negation. Once you know the case, you can predict whether the idiom dismisses, measures, accompanies or denies.

The second is derivation. хуйня adds the noun suffix -ня, which builds collectives and masses, so the word names stuff rather than an object; the same suffix appears in родня (rad-NYA), 'relatives', and болтовня (bal-tav-NYA), 'chatter'. хуёвина adds -ина, the suffix of single objects, so it names one thing. хуёвый adds -ёв- and the soft adjective ending, and хуёво is its neuter short form used adverbially. Every step is regular, and the regularity is what allows a learner to read a new form without a dictionary.

The third is desemanticisation. In the idioms the root no longer contributes its literal sense, and the phrase behaves as a single lexical item with its own argument structure. забить хуй на takes an accusative object introduced by на; хуй с ним takes a dative or instrumental participant; ни хуя negates whatever follows. Treating the root as meaningful inside these phrases produces nonsense, which is why the mistake section below is about reading strategies rather than about politeness.
depth.secondExample: A second exchange shows the family under pressure, at a kitchen table. «Ну и хуйня у тебя на кухне.» (noo ee khooy-NYA oo tee-BYA na KOO-khnye) 'What a mess you have in your kitchen.' The noun is the subject, the genitive у тебя marks the possessor, and the phrase ну и adds exasperation rather than a question. «Не хуёво живёшь.» (ne khoo-YO-va zhee-VYOSH) 'You are not doing badly for yourself.' Here the negated adverb understates a positive, which is a common ironic pattern: negating a negative evaluation produces praise. «А он, хуй, опять не пришёл.» (a on, KHUY, a-PYAT' ne pree-SHYOL) 'And he, the prick, did not turn up again.' This is the placeholder use in its contemptuous form, in apposition to он and set off by commas. Three sentences, three jobs: evaluation of a situation, ironic evaluation of a person's circumstances, and direct contempt for a person. A learner who can label the three will not mistake the third for the second.
depth.mistake:
The first error is mechanical translation of English 'fucking'. English uses a single intensifier across almost every syntactic position, and learners transfer that habit, inserting хуй or хуёвый wherever English would allow the expletive. Russian does not work that way: the family is lexically specific, each idiom has fixed arguments, and a form inserted by analogy usually produces something ungrammatical or unintentionally comic. The test is whether the phrase appears in a dictionary of idioms; if it does not, do not invent it.

The second error is choosing the wrong part of speech for an evaluation. Calling a film хуйня makes it junk, calling it хуёвый makes it bad as an adjective, and calling the filming хуёво criticises the manner. All three are possible and they are not interchangeable, because each answers a different question. The third error is treating the placeholder use as harmless. A native speaker can call a friend хуй in a tone that signals affection; a learner doing the same thing signals contempt, because the tone that licenses the word is not part of the learner's repertoire. Read the word, do not perform it.
depth.application: For reading, the family rewards attention to case. When you meet ни хуя, до хуя or на хуй, identify the case first and the meaning usually follows, because the preposition has already told you whether the phrase denies, measures or directs. For listening, the placeholder use is the one to train: when хуй appears where a noun should be, the sentence is about a person or a thing the speaker is dismissing, and the rest of the sentence tells you which. For production, the safe rule is to keep the family in your reading vocabulary and to use the neutral paraphrases from lesson 131 when you speak. That is not a moral position, it is a practical one: the idioms are fixed, the social licensing is delicate, and the cost of getting them wrong is paid by the speaker rather than by the sentence.
depth.summary: The хуй family is the largest in Russian mat and the most idiomatic. The noun declines like an inanimate masculine noun and often works as a contemptuous placeholder. хуйня names junk or an unspecified thing, хуёвина names a single object, хуёвый evaluates as bad and хуёво works both as a manner adverb and as a one-word predicate. The idioms are governed by case: ни хуя denies, до хуя measures, на хуй directs, хуй с ним dismisses, забить хуй на withdraws interest. The root is the most productive in the language and therefore one of the four that Russian media guidance bans outright, with all derivatives. Read the forms, learn the cases, and keep the evaluation out of your own speech until the audience is one you can read.

lessons.title: The пизда (peez-DA) family: a positive slang branch, a verb of stealing, and the line to пиздец
lessons.explanation:
This family is the clearest case in Russian mat of one root splitting into opposite evaluative branches. The noun пизда (peez-DA) is feminine, with genitive пизды (peez-DY), dative пизде (peez-DYE), accusative пизду (peez-DOO) and instrumental пиздой (peez-DOY). The English Wiktionary entry labels it both animate and inanimate, which reflects usage rather than uncertainty, and records the plural forms пи́зды and пёзды, the diminutive пиздёнка (peez-DYON-ka) and the augmentative пиздища (peez-DEE-shcha). It also records the texting spelling 3.14зда (tree-ee-chee-TY-re zda), in which pi stands in for the first syllable, a detail worth remembering when lesson 138 discusses censorship, because it shows that substitution is a recognised practice rather than a learner's invention.

Beyond the literal sense, the noun works as a one-word verdict on a situation: «Ну всё, пизда» (noo VSYO, peez-DA) means 'that is it, we are done for'. The grammar of that use is worth noticing. There is no verb, no copula and no subject beyond the situation itself, so the noun carries the whole predication, exactly as пиздец (peez-DYETS) does. The two words overlap in this function and differ in emphasis: пиздец is the terminal-state noun that ids 21 to 30 already introduced, and пизда as a verdict is blunter and more colloquial.

The positive branch is the part that catches learners. пиздатый (peez-DA-ty) means 'excellent, first-rate', and the Russian Wiktionary entry gives four senses: very good, of very good quality, reliable or trustworthy, and tasty or pleasant. It is a hard-stem adjective, so пиздатая (peez-DA-ta-ya), пиздатое (peez-DA-ta-ye) and пиздатые (peez-DA-ty-ye), with the stress fixed on the suffix. The suffix is -ат-, the one that builds adjectives of possession, as in бородатый (ba-ra-DA-ty), 'bearded'. Compositionally the word says 'endowed with' the noun, and the approving sense is a drift that Russian shares with several slang systems, where a taboo noun becomes a marker of excellence rather than of obscenity. The adverb and predicate пиздато (peez-DA-ta) follows the same pattern as хуёво: 'great, splendidly'. The Russian Wiktionary entry for пиздато lists отлично (at-LEECH-na), 'excellently', among its synonyms and gives хуёво as its antonym, which is the neatest evidence available that the two families have settled at opposite poles of the same evaluative scale.

The verb branch means stealing. спиздить (SPEEZ-deet') is perfective and transitive, 'to steal, to nick', with the present forms спизжу (SPEEZH-oo) and спиздишь (SPEEZ-deesh) and the past спиздил (SPEEZ-deel), спиздила (SPEEZ-dee-la). The imperfective is пиздить (PEEZ-deet'), which also has a separate sense 'to beat someone up', so the aspect pair is not perfectly symmetrical and context decides. The derivational link between the noun and the verb is traditional in the dictionaries but not demonstrated, and the English Wiktionary entry does not present a secure etymology; treat the connection as plausible and unproven, which is the same discipline lesson 131 applied to хуй.

The contrast with пиздец is the analytical point of the lesson. пиздец names a terminal state and evaluates downwards; пиздатый evaluates upwards; both descend from the same root and neither is predictable from it. That is why the family is a test of the reading method: a learner who assumes that an obscene root must produce an obscene evaluation will read пиздатый as an insult and miss the compliment entirely. The register does not become polite, however. All four of the words that Roskomnadzor's media guidance names are barred from Russian media together with their derivatives, so пиздатый is as unpublishable as пизда while meaning something much nicer.
lessons.example:
Three sentences, one root, three jobs. «Пиздато посидели.» (peez-DA-ta pa-see-DYE-lee) 'We had a great time sitting around.' The adverb modifies the past plural verb, and the whole sentence is warm rather than obscene in function. «У меня телефон спиздили в метро.» (oo mee-NYA tee-lee-FON SPEEZ-dee-lee f meet-RO) 'My phone was stolen on the metro.' The verb is perfective past plural with an impersonal third person plural, the phone is the accusative object, and the speaker does not say who did it. «Ну всё, пизда, автобус ушёл.» (noo VSYO, peez-DA, af-TO-boos oo-SHYOL) 'That is it, we are done for, the bus has gone.' The noun stands alone as a verdict between two clauses, with commas on both sides, and it agrees with nothing because it predicates nothing.

Now add the adjective and the contrast. «Пиздатый был концерт, только звук хуёвый.» (peez-DA-ty byl kan-TSERT, TOL'-ka zvook khoo-YO-vy) 'The concert was great, only the sound was crap.' Two evaluations in one sentence, one from the пизда family and one from the хуй family, and the pair is the ordinary way to praise and criticise in the same breath. «Пиздец, сколько работы.» (peez-DYETS, SKOL'-ka ra-BO-ty) 'It is a disaster how much work there is.' Here пиздец quantifies a burden rather than naming a catastrophe, which is the sense already taught at id 27. Read the four sentences together and the family looks less like a list of synonyms and more like a small evaluative system: пиздато approves, пизда condemns a situation, пиздец measures a burden, спиздить describes a theft.
lessons.question: A review says «Пиздатый фильм, но сюжет пиздец» (peez-DA-ty FEEl'm, no syu-ZHET peez-DYETS). What is the reviewer saying, and what is the common misreading?
lessons.answer: That the film is excellent but the plot is a disaster: пиздатый is strong praise and пиздец is strong condemnation, so the sentence is a mixed review.
lessons.distractor: That the film is obscene and the plot is a disaster, so the review is negative throughout.
lessons.correction: The misreading comes from assuming that an obscene root must carry a negative evaluation. пиздатый means 'excellent' and is used as praise; the Russian Wiktionary entry gives 'very good' and 'of very good quality' as its first senses, and the word functions as positive slang. пиздец means a terminal disaster and is negative. The two words share a root and sit at opposite ends of one scale, which is why the sentence can hold both without contradiction. The learner's error is semantic rather than grammatical: the sentence parses perfectly, and the failure is in the lexicon. Once the polarity of each branch is known, the mixed review reads naturally, and the same logic explains why пиздато appears in compliments while пиздец appears in complaints.

depth.definitions: Four terms organise the family. A positive slang item is a taboo word that has drifted into approval, and пиздатый is the standard Russian example. An adjective of possession is one built with -ат- that attributes the noun to its referent, as in бородатый 'bearded'; the approving sense of пиздатый is a later drift from that pattern. Aspect is the grammatical category that separates спиздить, a completed theft, from пиздить, the process, though the imperfective has an extra sense of beating that breaks the symmetry. A terminal-state noun is a noun that names an end point rather than an object, and пиздец is the clearest case in mat, with пизда used the same way in the blunt verdict «ну всё, пизда» (noo VSYO, peez-DA), 'that is it, we are done for'. Prerequisites are lesson 56 on aspect pairs, lesson 108 on adjective and adverb formation, and lesson 27, where пиздец was introduced.
depth.mechanism:
The derivational steps are ordinary and worth spelling out. The noun's stem is пизд-, and the stress sits on the ending, which is why the nominative is peez-DA and the genitive peez-DY. Add -ат- and an adjective ending and the stress moves to the suffix, giving peez-DA-ty; that stress shift is the phonetic signal that the word is an adjective rather than a noun with an ending. Add -о to the neuter short form and you get the adverb peez-DA-ta, which then functions as a predicate in the same way хуёво does. Add the prefix с- to the imperfective пиздить and you get a perfective verb of completion, in the pattern that lesson 106 described for с- with verbs of motion and transfer.

The semantic split is the interesting part. A suffix that means 'having X' can produce either a description or an evaluation, and which one it produces is a lexical fact about the pair. бородатый stays descriptive. пиздатый became evaluative because the noun it derives from names something speakers treat as quintessential, and the drift from 'endowed with the thing' to 'the real thing' to 'excellent' is a familiar path in slang. The same path does not operate on хуй, whose adjective хуёвый went the other way and means 'bad'. Two roots, the same suffix pattern, opposite outcomes: the lesson is that derivation predicts the grammar and the part of speech, and only partly predicts the value.
depth.secondExample: Take the family through its forms in one paragraph of invented speech, and parse as you go. «Он спиздил идею у соседа.» (on SPEEZ-deel ee-DYE-yu oo sa-SYE-da) 'He stole the idea from a neighbour.' The verb is perfective past masculine, the idea is the accusative object, and у plus genitive names the source. «Она пиздато готовит.» (a-NA peez-DA-ta ga-TO-veet) 'She cooks brilliantly.' The adverb modifies the third person verb, and the present tense is imperfective. «Пиздатая у тебя куртка.» (peez-DA-ta-ya oo tee-BYA KOORT-ka) 'That is a great jacket you have.' The adjective agrees with the feminine куртка, and the genitive у тебя marks possession while the jacket stays in the nominative. «Пиздец тебе будет.» (peez-DYETS tee-BYE BOO-deet) 'You are in for it.' The dative тебе marks the person affected and the future будет carries the prediction. Four forms, four grammatical jobs, and the only one aimed at a person is the last, which is a threat rather than an evaluation. That distinction between evaluating a thing and threatening a person is the bridge to lesson 136.
depth.mistake:
The first error is polarity. Learners hear an obscene root and assume contempt, so пиздатый is read as an insult and пиздато as sarcasm. Both are ordinary praise, and the mistake is expensive because it reverses the meaning of a compliment. The diagnostic is the syntactic frame: if the word agrees with a noun that the speaker likes, or modifies a verb describing something pleasant, the reading is positive.

The second error is register transfer in the other direction, assuming that positive meaning implies polite use. пиздатый is banned from Russian media exactly as пизда is, and saying it to a stranger is not a compliment but an obscenity with a compliment inside it. The third error is confusing спиздить with потерять (pa-tee-RYAT'), 'to lose'. The Russian verb names an agent and a completed act, so «я спиздил» (ya SPEEZ-deel), 'I stole it' is an admission, while «я потерял» (ya pa-tee-RYAL), 'I lost it' is a misfortune. Learners who use the two interchangeably produce confessions they did not intend.
depth.application: The practical skill is reading evaluation in comment threads and reviews, where пиздато and пиздатый appear constantly and where the polarity decides whether a recommendation is positive. Translate them neutrally as 'great' and 'excellent' and note the register separately, rather than translating the obscenity and losing the evaluation. For спиздить, the reading skill is aspect: a completed theft is perfective, a repeated or attempted one is imperfective, and the participle спизженный (SPEEZH-zhin-ny) works as an adjective for stolen goods. For production, keep the family passive. The positive branch is the most tempting to use because it sounds friendly, and it is also the branch where a learner's tone is most likely to be misread, because the licensing comes from the relationship rather than from the word.
depth.summary: The пизда family shows a root splitting into three functions. The noun names the body part and also serves as a blunt verdict on a situation. The adjective пиздатый and the adverb пиздато form the positive branch, meaning 'excellent' and 'great', with the stress fixed on the suffix; they are obscene in register and approving in meaning, which is the combination learners misread. спиздить is the perfective verb of stealing, with пиздить as its imperfective and an extra sense of beating that breaks the pair. пиздец, already taught, remains the terminal-state noun, and the contrast between пиздец and пиздатый is the clearest demonstration in the language that an obscene root does not fix an evaluation.

lessons.title: The ебать (ye-BAT', 'to fuck') family: the verb paradigm, the prefixes, ёбнутый and ёб твою мать
lessons.explanation:
The verb is the productive engine of Russian mat, and its paradigm is entirely regular once the stress pattern is understood. ебать (ye-BAT') is imperfective and transitive. The present is ебу (ye-BOO), ебёшь (ye-BYOSH), ебёт (ye-BYOT), ебём (ye-BYOM), ебёте (ye-BYO-tye), ебут (ye-BOOT); the past is ебал (ye-BAL), ебала (ye-BA-la), ебало (ye-BA-la) and ебали (ye-BA-lee); the imperative is еби (ye-BEE). The letter ё appears in every form where the vowel is stressed and disappears where it is not, which is why the first person singular and the third person plural have a plain е while the second person singular has ё. Nothing about the conjugation is irregular, and a learner who can conjugate нести (nees-TEE), 'to carry', can conjugate this verb.

The English Wiktionary entry supplies the aspect partners and the derived forms in one place: the perfectives are выебать (VY-ye-bat'), отъебать (at-ye-BAT') and поебать (pa-YE-bat'), the semelfactive is ёбнуть (YOB-noot'), the verbal noun is ебля (YEB-lya), and the verbal adjectives are ёбаный (YO-ba-ny), ебучий (ye-BOO-chee) and ебейший (ye-BYE-shee). A semelfactive is a verb that names a single act rather than a process, and ёбнуть is the one that generates ёбнутый, which is why the participle and the semelfactive belong in the same lesson.

The reflexive form changes the argument structure. ебаться (ye-BAT-sa) is intransitive or reciprocal, 'to fuck, to have sex', with no object in the accusative. In colloquial usage it also takes с plus the instrumental to mean 'to struggle with something', as in ебаться с компьютером (ye-BAT-sa s kam-PYOO-te-ram), 'to wrestle with a computer', and that sense is the source of a great deal of ordinary complaint. The -ся is doing exactly the work lesson 105 described for свой: it points the action back at the subject and removes the external object.

The prefixed perfectives divide the labour. заебать (za-ye-BAT') means to wear someone out, to exhaust or bore them to the point of exasperation, and it is transitive with the person in the accusative: ты меня заебал (ty mee-NYA za-ye-BAL), 'you have worn me out'. The noun заёб (za-YOB) names the resulting nuisance. выебать has two senses in the Russian Wiktionary entry: the literal one, to have sex with someone to completion, and a second one, to swear at someone severely or to punish them harshly. The second sense is the one that appears in professional and domestic arguments, and it is why the verb can be used about a person without any sexual meaning at all. отъебать and поебать cover completion and a bounded episode, and поебать in the dative construction, мне поебать (mnye pa-YE-bat'), means 'I could not care less'.

ёбнутый (YOB-noo-ty) is a participle that has become an adjective. The verb ёбнуть means to strike or bang, and the participle describes someone who has been struck, which is the metaphor behind the slang sense 'unhinged, crazy, not right in the head'. The Russian Wiktionary entry gives 'strange, insane, crazy, abnormal' and lists ебанутый (ye-ba-NOO-ty) as a variant. The feminine is ёбнутая (YOB-noo-ta-ya), and the word is used about people and about ideas, as in ёбнутая идея (YOB-noo-ta-ya ee-DYE-ya), 'a deranged idea'. Because it is an adjective of condition rather than a verb, it agrees with its noun and can be used predicatively with a copula that Russian usually leaves out.

The fixed interjection ёб твою мать (YOB tva-YU MAT') is the phrase that Russian linguistics treats as the canonical formula of mat. Boris Uspensky's analysis, summarised in the Russian Wikipedia article, reconstructs an earlier form with тебе rather than твою and argues that the original subject was a dog, so that the phrase asserted that the addressee was a dog invited to copulate with its mother; he cites a Church Slavonic charter of the Wallachian hospodar Alexander Aldi from 1432, Herberstein's sixteenth-century account, and the expression лая матерная (LA-ya ma-TYER-na-ya), 'mat barking', as evidence. That reconstruction is a scholarly hypothesis, not a settled etymology, and it should be reported as such. What is certain is the modern function: the phrase is an expletive of exasperation, it is not addressed to anyone's mother, and it can be uttered with no addressee at all.

Register is uniform across the family. All of these forms are mat, all are barred from Russian media under the guidance that names the obscene verb and its derivatives, and all are far more frequent in speech than in writing. The verb is also the one mat root that English speakers overestimate, because English 'fuck' has a wider syntactic range than ебать: English allows the participle as a general intensifier in almost any noun phrase, while Russian prefers the adjectives ёбаный and ебучий in a much narrower set of collocations.
lessons.example:
An invented argument in a shared kitchen, parsed line by line. «Ты меня заебал со своей музыкой.» (ty mee-NYA za-ye-BAL sa sva-YEY MOO-zee-koy) 'You have worn me out with your music.' The person worn out is in the accusative, the cause is introduced by с plus the instrumental, and the verb is perfective past masculine. «Да я не виноват, что соседи ёбнутые.» (da ya ne vee-na-VAT, shta sa-SYE-dee YOB-noo-ty-ye) 'It is not my fault the neighbours are deranged.' The adjective agrees with the plural соседи, and the clause is predicative with no copula. «Ёб твою мать, опять эта сигнализация.» (YOB tva-YU MAT', a-PYAT' EH-ta seem-ga-lee-ZA-tsee-ya) 'For fuck's sake, that alarm again.' The interjection stands outside the syntax of the sentence, separated by a comma, and nothing in the rest of the clause depends on it.

Now the ambiguity that matters for reading. «Он выебал меня за опоздание.» (on VY-ye-bal mee-NYA za a-paz-DA-nee-ye) 'He tore me off a strip for being late.' The literal reading is available in principle, and the preposition за plus the accusative of reason selects the second sense, the severe telling-off. Compare it with «Он выебал её» (on VY-ye-bal ye-YO), with no reason phrase, where the literal sense is the default and the sentence is a statement about sex. The lesson is that выебать is disambiguated by its complements, not by its form, and a reader who has only one gloss for the verb will misread one of the two sentences. One more form: «Я заебался.» (ya za-ye-BAL-sya) 'I am worn out.' The -ся removes the object and the subject becomes the exhausted person, which is the reverse of the first sentence in this paragraph.
lessons.question: One colleague says «Ты меня заебал» (ty mee-NYA za-ye-BAL) and another says «Я заебался» (ya za-ye-BAL-sya). Who is worn out in each sentence?
lessons.answer: In the first, the speaker is worn out by the addressee, who is the object; in the second, the speaker is worn out, with no object at all.
lessons.distractor: Both sentences describe the same situation, because -ся is only a stylistic variant with no effect on meaning.
lessons.correction: The error is to treat -ся as decoration. The suffix removes the accusative object and redirects the action at the subject, which is the same mechanism that turns мыть (MYT'), 'to wash something', into мыться (MYT-sa), 'to wash oneself'. So заебать takes the exhausted person in the accusative, while заебаться has that person as its subject. The two sentences describe opposite role assignments in the same event, and a learner who hears only one of them will report the wrong person as the victim of the exhaustion. The diagnostic is the case of the first noun after the verb: an accusative pronoun such as меня marks the person worn out, and its absence with -ся marks the speaker as the one who is worn out.

depth.definitions: Five terms carry the family. Transitivity is the property that lets заебать take an accusative object, and its absence with -ся is what reverses the roles. Aspect separates the imperfective ебать from the perfectives выебать, отъебать and поебать, and the choice of aspect decides whether the sentence describes a process or a completed act. A semelfactive verb names a single occurrence of an action, and ёбнуть is the semelfactive of this root, which is why it patterns with a bang or a blow rather than with a process. A participle used as an adjective is a verb form that has taken on the agreement and function of an adjective, and ёбнутый is the standard case. A fixed interjection is a phrase that functions as a single emotional token and takes no arguments, and ёб твою мать is the canonical example. Prerequisites are lesson 56 on aspect, lesson 105 on reflexivity and свой, and lesson 109 on evaluative suffixes.
depth.mechanism:
The paradigm is driven by stress and by one stem. The stem is еб-, and the present endings are those of the first conjugation: -у, -ёшь, -ёт, -ём, -ёте, -ут. The ё is written only under stress, so the second person singular and the third person singular and plural carry it while the first person singular and the first person plural do not; Russian orthography does not write ё in unstressed syllables. The past tense uses the infinitive stem plus -л and the gender endings, giving ебал, ебала, ебало and ебали, with the stress staying on the final syllable throughout.

Prefixation changes the aspect and the argument structure together. за- adds saturation and produces a perfective verb whose object is the person saturated. вы- adds completion and produces a perfective verb whose object may be a person or a thing, and whose second sense extends completion into the idea of finishing someone off verbally. от- adds separation and completion. по- adds a bounded episode. In each case the prefix is the same morpheme that lesson 106 described for ordinary verbs, and the mat root behaves like any other root.

The reflexive suffix is the third mechanism. -ся removes the accusative object and either makes the verb intransitive, as in ебаться, or redirects it at the subject, as in заебаться. The same suffix turns ёбнуть into ёбнуться, 'to bang oneself, to fall hard' and, figuratively, 'to lose one's mind'. Participles then form on the semelfactive stem with -т-, giving ёбнутый, which agrees like an adjective and can be used attributively or predicatively.
depth.secondExample:
Two more forms, both common and both easy to misread. «Эта музыка меня заебала.» (EH-ta MOO-zee-ka mee-NYA za-ye-BA-la) 'This music has worn me out.' The verb agrees with the feminine subject музыка, and the person worn out is the accusative меня; the agreement is with the thing that does the wearing out, not with the person, which is the opposite of the English intuition. «Он ёбнулся с лестницы.» (on YOB-nool-sya s LYEST-nee-tsy) 'He fell off the ladder, hard.' Here the verb is reflexive, the subject is the person who fell, and с plus the genitive names the surface he fell from; the figurative sense, 'he lost it', is available without the phrase and is selected by context.

A third form shows the noun. «Меня достал этот заёб с отчётами.» (mee-NYA das-TAL EH-tat za-YOB s at-CHYO-ta-mee) 'I am sick of this nuisance with the reports.' The noun is the subject, the verb достал (das-TAL), 'got to me', is the predicate, and с plus instrumental names the domain. Note that the noun and the verb are not interchangeable: заёб names the nuisance, заебать names the effect on a person, and a learner who uses the noun where the verb belongs produces a sentence that is grammatical and odd. That pattern, a noun for the thing and a verb for the effect, repeats across the whole family and is the practical reason to learn the forms in pairs.
depth.mistake:
The first error is to treat ёб твою мать as a threat. It is an expletive of exasperation, uttered at a broken alarm or a missed bus, and it has no addressee and no literal content in use. A learner who hears it as a curse on someone's mother will misjudge the speaker's intention and the social temperature, which is usually mild frustration rather than aggression.

The second error is aspect and transitivity. Learners use заебать when they mean заебаться, producing a sentence that blames the listener for the speaker's fatigue, and they use выебать for the telling-off sense without the complements that select it. Both errors are grammatical sentences with the wrong roles, which is the hardest kind of mistake to notice in one's own speech. The third error is tonal. заебал is one of the most frequent expressions of exasperation among close colleagues and friends, and it is also a direct obscenity aimed at a person; the same string of sounds is a joke in one relationship and an insult in another. The word does not carry the answer, the relationship does, which is the subject of lesson 137.
depth.application: For reading, the family rewards attention to the object. If the person is in the accusative, the verb describes an effect on them; if there is no object and the verb has -ся, the subject is the affected party. That single test resolves most of the ambiguity in the prefixed perfectives. For listening, ёбнутый and its variants are the most frequent adjectives in the family, and they are usually descriptive rather than hostile: calling an idea ёбнутая is closer to 'wild' than to an insult, though the register stays obscene. For production, the family is best kept passive. The expletive is the form learners are most tempted to imitate because it is memorable, and it is also the form that most reliably marks a speaker as either fluent or inappropriate, with very little middle ground.
depth.summary: The ебать family is the productive core of Russian mat. The verb conjugates regularly, with ё written only under stress, and its aspect partners выебать, отъебать and поебать divide the work of completion and bounded episode. The reflexive ебаться removes the object and can mean either having sex or struggling with something. Prefixes assign roles: заебать wears a person out, выебать completes an act or delivers a severe telling-off, and заёб names the resulting nuisance. ёбнуть is the semelfactive, and its participle ёбнутый is the ordinary adjective for 'unhinged'. ёб твою мать is a fixed expletive whose etymology is a scholarly hypothesis and whose modern function is exasperation, not a threat.

lessons.title: блядь and блять (BLYAT'): one spelling for a noun and an interjection, and the softening chain
lessons.explanation:
блядь (BLYAT') is the only root in the mat core that names neither a body part nor an act, and that difference explains almost everything about how it behaves. As a noun it is feminine, belongs to the third declension with a soft sign, and declines бляди (BLYA-dee) genitive, бляди dative, блядь accusative, блядью (BLYA-d'yo) instrumental, бляди prepositional, with plural бляди and genitive plural блядей (blya-DYE). The sense is 'whore, slut', and the Russian Wikipedia article records that Plucer-Sarno placed it second among mat lexemes in his surveys, behind ебать but ahead of the anatomical roots, because speakers recognise it as mat instantly. Its use as a noun is a serious gendered insult, and it is aimed at a person; nothing in the grammar of the word is unusual, and everything in its social force is.

The interjection is written the same way and behaves completely differently. It expresses exasperation, dismay or emphasis, it takes no arguments, it agrees with nothing, and it stands outside the syntax of the clause, usually set off by a comma or uttered alone. The English Wiktionary entry records the variants бля (BLYA), блять (BLYAT') and бляха (BLYA-kha) under the interjection, together with the texting forms блд and блт. A word that takes no arguments and agrees with nothing is doing the work of a particle rather than the work of a noun, and lesson 102's treatment of же (ZHE) and ведь (VYET') is the right comparison: the function is stance marking, not reference.

The spelling question follows from that split. The noun needs the soft sign because it is a third declension feminine noun, like ночь (NOCH'), 'night', and дверь (DVYER'), 'door'. The interjection inherits the spelling from the noun, so the dictionary form is блядь in both functions, and the English Wiktionary entry for блять labels it 'misspelling of блядь' with the labels vulgar and slang. That is a prescriptive verdict, not a description of usage: блять is extremely common in informal writing, many writers use it deliberately to mark the interjection as distinct from the noun, and some style guides tolerate it for that reason. The pronunciation is identical, since the soft sign does not add a sound in this position; the difference is orthographic, and the safest course in formal writing is the dictionary spelling, блядь.

The softening chain is the other half of the lesson. бля is the clipped form, still obscene, used as a lighter exclamation. бляха (BLYA-kha) is a real noun meaning 'buckle plate, badge', and the English Wiktionary entry records that it is also used as a minced oath, especially in the phrase бляха-муха (BLYA-kha MOO-kha). блин (BLEEN) is the word for a pancake and is the mildest rung of the chain, already introduced at id 21. The three substitutes work because each is a genuine word that shares the opening consonant cluster with the taboo item, so the hearer recognises the shape of the replaced word while hearing something publishable. That is the definition of a minced oath, and lesson 138 generalises it across the whole lexicon.

Functionally, the noun and the interjection sit at opposite ends of the targeting scale. The noun assigns a predicate to a person, usually a woman, and the assignment is the insult. The interjection assigns nothing to anyone; it reports the speaker's state. Two sentences with the same spelling make the difference visible: «Ты блядь, а не подруга» (ty BLYAT', a ne pad-ROO-ga), 'you are a whore, not a friend', where the noun is the predicate of ты and the contrast with подруга completes the insult; and «Блядь, я забыл ключи» (BLYAT', ya za-BYL KLYOO-chee), 'damn, I forgot the keys', where the word stands outside the clause and the clause is a complete statement without it. Remove the noun from the first sentence and the sentence collapses; remove the interjection from the second and the sentence survives with a flatter tone. That removal test is the most reliable diagnostic in this whole unit.

Register is uniform only in the legal sense. Both functions are obscene by the media definition, since Roskomnadzor's guidance names the obscene word for a woman of loose behaviour together with all derivatives, and both are barred from broadcast and from the press. Socially they diverge sharply: the interjection passes between colleagues who would never use the noun at a person, and the noun can end a friendship. A learner who treats the two as one word with two meanings will use the wrong one, so this lesson keeps them as two lexical items that happen to share a spelling.
lessons.example:
Four lines, read aloud in order, with the function of the word marked in each. «Блядь, опять дождь.» (BLYAT', a-PYAT' DOSHT') 'Damn, rain again.' The interjection is initial, comma-separated, and the clause опять дождь is a complete impersonal statement; nothing in it depends on the first word. «Блядь, ну сколько можно.» (BLYAT', noo SKOL'-ka MOZH-na) 'For heaven's sake, how long can this go on.' Again initial and comma-separated, and here the interjection carries the exasperation that the rhetorical question alone would not.

Now the noun. «Она мне не подруга, она блядь.» (a-NA mnye ne pad-ROO-ga, a-NA BLYAT') 'She is not my friend, she is a whore.' The noun is the predicate of она, the pronoun is repeated for emphasis, and the sentence is a judgement of a person. «Ты блядь.» (ty BLYAT') 'You are a whore.' Two words, no verb, copula omitted as Russian normally omits it in the present, and the whole utterance is the insult. The minimal pair with the first line is the lesson: same spelling, same pronunciation, one word aimed at nobody and one word aimed at somebody.

Add the chain and the contrast is complete. «Бляха-муха, забыл пропуск.» (BLYA-kha MOO-kha, za-BYL PRO-poosk) 'Darn it, I forgot my pass.' The substitute is a real noun used as an exclamation, and the register is mild enough for an office. «Блин, ну что за день.» (BLEEN, noo SHTA za DYEN') 'Darn, what a day.' The mildest rung, and the one a learner can use in almost any company. Between блядь and блин there are two intermediate steps, бля and бляха, and the choice among them is a choice of audience rather than a choice of meaning, which is exactly the ladder lesson 138 will formalise.
lessons.question: Two messages arrive. One says «Ты блядь» (ty BLYAT'), the other says «Блядь, я опоздал» (BLYAT', ya a-paz-DAL). Which one is an insult with a target, and what is the evidence?
lessons.answer: The first: there the word is the predicate of ты and judges a person, while in the second it stands outside the clause as an exclamation about the speaker's own lateness.
lessons.distractor: Both, because the word is obscene in either position and obscenity always targets someone.
lessons.correction: Obscenity and targeting are different properties, and this pair separates them. In «Ты блядь» (ty BLYAT'), 'you are a whore' the word is the predicate of a second person pronoun with no verb, so the sentence asserts something about the hearer; remove it and nothing remains. In «Блядь, я опоздал» (BLYAT', ya a-paz-DAL), 'damn, I am late' the word is comma-separated, the clause я опоздал is complete without it, and the only person evaluated is the speaker. The learner's error is to infer intention from the taboo rather than from the syntax. The same test works for the whole family: if the clause survives the removal of the word and the word stands outside the commas, it is an expletive, and if the clause collapses, it was doing grammatical work and probably aimed at someone.

depth.definitions: Four terms carry the lesson. A noun is a word that names an entity and takes case and number, and блядь as a noun does exactly that. An interjection is a word or phrase that expresses a state and enters into no syntactic relation, and the same string of letters serves as one. A discourse particle is a word that marks the speaker's stance toward what follows, and the interjection belongs to that functional family even though it is lexically obscene; lesson 102 treated the neutral members of the family. A minced oath is a harmless word substituted for a taboo one, usually similar in sound, and бляха and блин are the Russian examples. Prerequisites are lesson 34 on the third declension, lesson 102 on particles, and lesson 21, where блин was introduced.
depth.mechanism:
The soft sign is the visible trace of the noun's declension class. Third declension feminines end in a soft consonant written with ь, and they take -и in the genitive, dative and prepositional singular; that is why the paradigm is бляди, бляди, блядь, блядью, бляди rather than the -а pattern of земля. The interjection takes the same letters because it was recruited from the noun, and once recruited it stopped declining: there is no genitive of an exclamation.

The interjection's syntax is defined by what it does not do. It does not agree, it does not govern a case, it does not occupy an argument slot, and it can be repeated or combined with other exclamations without changing the truth conditions of the sentence. Prosodically it is set off by a pause and usually carries a falling tone, which is why the comma in writing is not optional decoration but a representation of the prosody. That is also why the removal test works: an element that the clause can lose without becoming ungrammatical was never part of the clause.

The minced oath mechanism is phonetic. бляха and блин preserve the initial cluster bl- and the single syllable shape, so the hearer's recognition of the taboo word is triggered while the actual word is a buckle or a pancake. The substitution works only because both are real words with their own meanings, which is why they can appear in print where the original cannot. A substitute that is not a word, such as a string of asterisks, does not have this property and is treated by regulators as the original, which lesson 138 takes up.
depth.secondExample:
Take the abstract noun and the adjective, which are the forms a reader meets most often after the interjection. блядство (BLYAT-stva) is the abstract noun from the same stem, naming whoring or, colloquially, a state of sleaze and disorder; it is neuter and declines like дело (DYE-la), 'matter'. блядский (BLYAT-skee) is the adjective, 'whorish' in the literal sense and 'damned, bloody' in the expressive sense, declining like русский (ROOS-keey). «Ну и блядство тут у вас.» (noo ee BLYAT-stva toot oo VAS) 'What a sleazy mess you have here.' The noun is the predicate, тут is the locative, and у вас marks whose mess it is. «Блядский автобус опять не пришёл.» (BLYAT-skee af-TO-boos a-PYAT' ne pree-SHYOL) 'The bloody bus did not come again.' The adjective agrees with the masculine автобус and evaluates the thing rather than a person.

Put the four functions in a row and the family is complete: noun aimed at a woman, interjection aimed at nobody, abstract noun naming a state, adjective evaluating a thing. Only the first is an insult in the strict sense, and only the first requires a person as its target. A learner who can place a form in that row has understood the lesson, and a learner who cannot will keep hearing insults where the speaker is only tired of the weather.
depth.mistake:
The first error is orthographic and social at once: writing блять in a formal message because it looks like the interjection. Dictionaries list it as a misspelling, editors correct it, and the correction draws attention to the word in exactly the context where the writer wanted it to pass unnoticed. Use блядь if the word must appear at all, and prefer the substitutes from the chain in any writing that will be read by someone who did not choose to read it.

The second error is the target error. Learners hear the interjection constantly, conclude that the word is socially acceptable, and then use the noun at a person. The two are the same letters and different speech acts, and the tolerance extended to the expletive does not extend to the insult. The third error is to treat the substitutes as synonyms. бляха and блин are separate lexical items with their own grammar, so «блин» (BLEEN), 'pancake, darn' cannot be used as a predicate of a person, and «бляха» (BLYA-kha), 'buckle plate' in its buckle sense has nothing to do with any of this. The chain maps register onto form; it does not create equivalents.
depth.application: For reading, the practical skill is to notice the comma. A comma-separated блядь at the start of a clause is an expletive, and a блядь that occupies a predicate slot is an insult; subtitles and comment threads supply hundreds of examples, and the pattern becomes automatic quickly. For writing, the dictionary spelling is блядь in both functions, and the substitutes are the register-safe options. For listening, the interjection is often reduced to бля or even to a single consonant in fast speech, which is why learners sometimes miss it entirely and then wonder what the emotional temperature of the conversation was. For production, the noun is the form to avoid without exception, and the interjection is the form to recognise rather than to imitate until the company is one where you have heard it used first.
depth.summary: блядь is one spelling with two grammatical lives. As a noun it is a third declension feminine with the paradigm бляди, бляди, блядь, блядью and the sense 'whore', and it is a serious insult aimed at a person. As an interjection it takes no arguments, agrees with nothing and stands outside the clause, expressing exasperation. The spelling блять is listed by dictionaries as a misspelling of the same word, though it is common in informal writing; the pronunciation is identical. The softening chain runs блядь, бля, бляха, блин, and each step replaces the taboo item with a real word of similar shape. The removal test separates the two functions, and the audience decides which rung of the chain is available.
