questions.prompt: Two phrases arrive in the same conversation: «Ну ты и хуй» (noo ty ee KHUY) and «Ну и хуй с ним» (noo ee KHUY s NEEM). Which one is invective, and what is the grammatical evidence?
questions.answer: The first: the noun is the predicate of ты, so the hearer is the target. The second is a fixed dismissal with с plus the instrumental, and the person is being written off rather than addressed.
questions.distractor: Both, because the same obscene noun and the same exasperated particle ну appear in each.
questions.correction: The error is to read force off the vocabulary instead of the syntax. In «Ну ты и хуй» (noo ty ee KHUY), 'you really are a prick' the second person pronoun is the subject and the noun is its predicate, so the sentence assigns a property to the hearer. In «Ну и хуй с ним» (noo ee KHUY s NEEM), 'to hell with him' the pronoun is ним in the instrumental governed by с, the phrase is fixed, and nobody is being addressed. Identical particles and identical nouns produce two different speech acts, which is why lesson 136 classifies by target first and by word second. The practical consequence is that the first requires the response repertoire of lesson 139 and the second requires none.

questions.prompt: A learner tells a mat joke at a pub with friends, where it is received well, then repeats it an hour later to a stranger who has bumped into him. What has changed, and why does the second telling carry a different risk?
questions.answer: The licence has gone: among friends the obscenity signals affiliation, while at a stranger the only available function is lowering status, which reads as aggression and can escalate in a public place.
questions.distractor: Nothing important has changed, because the joke and the intention are the same in both settings.
questions.correction: The error is to locate meaning in the words rather than in the relationship. Zhelvis's taxonomy, summarised in the Russian Wikipedia article on обсценная лексика (ap-STSEN-na-ya LEK-see-ka), 'obscene vocabulary', includes contact between equals and the lowering of an addressee's status as separate functions. The first requires shared history and roughly equal standing; the second requires neither, and it is the only one available with a stranger. In a public place the escalation can also become an administrative matter, since article 20.1 treats public obscenity as petty hooliganism. Intention is not a defence, because the hearer has no access to it.

questions.prompt: You are writing a short item for a student newspaper that will carry a 16+ marking. A quoted source said «Пиздец, сколько работы» (peez-DYETS, SKOL'-ka ra-BO-ty). Which version can you print, and why?
questions.answer: Пипец, сколько работы (pee-PYETS, SKOL'-ka ra-BO-ty): пипец is the euphemistic substitute and sits on the permitted side of the media rule, while пиздец and its derivatives are barred outright.
questions.distractor: Пиздец with the middle letters replaced by asterisks, because masking removes the obscenity while keeping the quotation accurate.
questions.correction: The error is to treat masking as substitution. Roskomnadzor's guidance, summarised in the Wikipedia article on мат, bars the four obscene items and all derivatives, and states that replacing letters with ellipsis does not remove liability, while a formulation such as 'the word beginning with b' is acceptable because it does not reproduce the word. Asterisks reproduce the word for every reader and leave the writer exposed. пипец is recorded by English Wiktionary as a euphemistic and vulgar substitute for пиздец, and it is permitted with an age marking, though it still reads as swearing, which is why a direct quotation of the plain statement would be better still.

questions.prompt: A colleague has just sworn at you in front of the team. You want to keep the limit and avoid a scene. Which reply does that, and why is it the firmest of the four phrases?
questions.answer: «Я не понял. Ты это мне?» (ya ne PO-nyal. ty EH-ta mnye), 'I did not catch that. Is that aimed at me?': it is a repair move that forces the speaker to repeat or withdraw in front of the audience.
questions.distractor: «Не надо так» (nee NA-da tak), 'don't do that', because it names the behaviour and therefore sets the clearest boundary.
questions.correction: не надо так is a real boundary and it is the softest of the four, because it is impersonal and can sound supervisory, as if you were correcting a child; it works best from a position of some authority. я не понял is firmer because it is a repair move: it asks for repetition, which makes the speaker the author of the words a second time and gives them a face-saving way out. The choice between «Ты это мне?» (ty EH-ta mnye) with ты and «Это мне?» (EH-ta mnye) without it also decides how much intimacy you accept. The error to avoid is matching the obscenity, which converts a one-sided attack into a mutual exchange in front of witnesses.

questions.prompt: A colleague writes in a work chat «Да блядь, я вчера отправил» (da BLYAT', ya fchee-RA at-PRA-veel). Classify the obscenity, then say what changes if a manager joins the chat.
questions.answer: It is an expletive with no target, because it is comma-separated and the clause survives without it; the manager's arrival changes the register, not the target or the force, because the obscenity becomes part of an institutional record.
questions.distractor: It is invective aimed at the reader, and the manager's arrival changes nothing because the participants are the same.
questions.correction: The error is to classify by word rather than by frame. The removal test settles the first label: take блядь out and «я вчера отправил» (ya fchee-RA at-PRA-veel), 'I sent it yesterday', is a complete clause, so the word was never doing grammatical work against the hearer. Target and force are therefore nobody and expletive. The register question is separate and it is the one the manager's arrival changes: a written workplace channel now has an institutional reader who did not consent to the tone, and the message persists. A learner who labels this as invective will respond as if attacked and miss the actual problem, which is the channel rather than the target.

questions.prompt: Which present-tense form of ебать (ye-BAT') is written with ё, and why?
questions.answer: Ебёшь (ye-BYOSH) and the other forms stressed on the ending are written with ё, because Russian writes ё only when the vowel is stressed.
questions.distractor: Ебу (ye-BOO), because the first person singular always carries the stressed vowel.
questions.correction: The error is to assume that the first person is the stressed form. The stress in this verb sits on the ending throughout the present, and ё is written only where that stressed vowel is the one in question, which is why ебёшь, ебёт, ебём and ебёте have ё while ебу and ебут have a plain е. The same rule explains почему (pa-chee-MOO), 'why', without ё and что (SHTO), 'what', without it. This is ordinary Russian orthography rather than something specific to mat, and lesson 134 treats it as the first thing to fix because a learner who writes ёбу has written a form that does not exist.

questions.prompt: Why is the phrase ни хуя (nee khoo-YA) in the genitive rather than the accusative?
questions.answer: Because ни is a negator that governs the genitive, so 'not a fucking thing' appears as 'not of a prick'.
questions.distractor: Because хуй (KHUY) is animate in this construction, and animate nouns take the genitive for the accusative.
questions.correction: The error is to reach for animacy. хуй is treated as inanimate, which is why its accusative repeats the nominative, so the genitive here cannot come from animacy. It comes from ни, the negator that takes the genitive in categorical denials, exactly as in ни слова (nee SLO-va), 'not a word', and ни шагу (nee SHA-goo), 'not a step'. Once the case is identified, the meaning follows: the phrase denies the existence of even one instance. The same logic explains why до хуя (da khoo-YA) is genitive too, since до governs the genitive for extent, which is why both idioms look alike and mean opposite things.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to say 'with a cunt' in the instrumental and writes «пиздой» (peez-DOY). Is that right, and what does the paradigm predict?
questions.answer: Yes: the noun is feminine with stress on the ending, so the instrumental is пиздой (peez-DOY), and the dative is пизде (peez-DYE).
questions.distractor: No: the instrumental should follow the third declension and end in -ью, as in ночь (NOCH'), 'night'.
questions.correction: The error is to apply the third declension to a first declension noun. пизда belongs to the -а class, like вода (va-DA), 'water', whose instrumental is водой (va-DOY), so the instrumental is пиздой with the same ending and the same stress pattern. The third declension ending -ью belongs to nouns such as ночь (NOCH'), 'night', which have no -а in the nominative. A learner who confuses the two classes will produce forms that are recognisable and wrong, and the error will spread to every derived form, which is why lesson 133 treats the paradigm as the foundation rather than as a detail.

questions.prompt: What is the difference in force between хуйня (khooy-NYA) and хуйло (khooy-LO)?
questions.answer: хуйня is a mass noun evaluating stuff, 'junk, nonsense', while хуйло is an agent noun naming a contemptible person.
questions.distractor: They are synonyms, differing only in the speaker's regional accent.
questions.correction: The error is to ignore the suffix. -ня builds nouns of mass or collectivity, the same suffix as in родня (rad-NYA), 'relatives', so хуйня evaluates a substance, a category or a situation. -ло builds contemptuous person nouns, so хуйло (khooy-LO) names somebody and is grammatically neuter, declining хуйла (KHUY-la) in the genitive. The difference is not stylistic but grammatical: one can be the subject of «это хуйня» (EH-ta khooy-NYA), 'this is junk', and the other cannot without changing the sentence's target. Lesson 136 uses the pair to show that the suffix decides what kind of thing is being evaluated, which is a more reliable guide than the obscenity of the root.

questions.prompt: A learner adds a diminutive to a mat noun and concludes the result is safe to use in polite company. What is wrong with that reasoning?
questions.answer: Diminutives change stance, not register: пиздёнка (peez-DYON-ka) is still obscene, and the diminutive can sound affectionate, ironic or patronising depending on tone.
questions.distractor: Nothing is wrong: diminutives are the standard Russian way of making a word polite.
questions.correction: The error is to transfer the softening that diminutives perform on ordinary nouns, such as стол (STOL), 'table', to стол-ик (STO-leek), 'little table', onto a root whose taboo is lexical. The diminutive changes how the speaker presents the referent, which is a matter of stance, and it leaves the obscenity exactly where it was. The English Wiktionary entry for пизда records пиздёнка as the diminutive and пиздища as the augmentative, and neither is publishable. Lesson 109 taught the evaluative suffixes as a system for stance; this lesson applies the same analysis to mat and finds that the legal and social position of the word does not move.

questions.prompt: Which test reliably separates the noun блядь from the interjection блядь in a sentence?
questions.answer: The removal test: if the clause survives without the word and the word stands outside the commas, it is an interjection; if the clause collapses, the word was the predicate and the noun.
questions.distractor: The spelling: блядь is the noun and блять is the interjection.
questions.correction: The spelling is not a reliable test, because dictionaries list блять as a misspelling of the same word and the pronunciation is identical in both functions. The removal test works because it is a syntactic test: an interjection agrees with nothing, governs nothing and can be deleted without damage, while a predicate noun cannot be deleted without destroying the sentence. «Блядь, я опоздал» (BLYAT', ya a-paz-DAL), 'damn, I am late', survives deletion; «Ты блядь» (ty BLYAT'), 'you are a whore', does not. The learner's error is to look for a lexical difference where the difference is grammatical, and the consequence is misjudging whether a person has been insulted.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the origin of хуй (KHUY) is safe to make in an essay?
questions.answer: That the origin is unknown, and that the academic etymological dictionary connects the word with хвоя (KHVO-ya), 'pine needles', while other scholars propose different roots.
questions.distractor: That the word descends from a Tatar root, as most linguists agree.
questions.correction: The error is to repeat a confident derivation without a source. The Russian Wikipedia article on the word begins by stating that the exact origin is unknown, then reports the connection with хвоя from the Этимологический словарь славянских языков, Kovalyov's reconstruction of a common Slavic *XŪ meaning 'offshoot', a link to the Indo-European root *skēu-, 'to be sharp', and Illich-Svitych's Nostratic proposal, which the article itself notes most linguists reject. A Tatar origin is a common folk claim and it is not what the cited sources say. The safe formulation names the uncertainty, names the dictionary and labels the contested proposals as contested, which is the discipline lesson 131 sets out.

questions.prompt: A blogger writes «п***ц» (peez-DYETS, letters masked) to avoid the media rules. What does the regulator's guidance say about that, and what is the actual safe option?
questions.answer: That replacing letters with ellipsis does not remove liability, while a formulation such as 'the word beginning with b' does, because it does not reproduce the word.
questions.distractor: That masking is acceptable, because the obscenity is no longer visible on the page.
questions.correction: The error is to think of censorship as typography. Roskomnadzor's guidance, summarised in the Wikipedia article on мат, names the four obscene items and all their derivatives, states that letter substitution with ellipsis does not remove liability, and permits naming the initial letter instead precisely because the word is not reproduced. The social logic runs the same way: readers reconstruct masked forms instantly, so the emphasis survives while the deniability does not. The genuinely safe options are the euphemisms from lesson 138, which are separate words, and the neutral paraphrase, which carries the information without any register at all.

questions.prompt: A stranger at a station swears at you and uses ты. You want distance rather than a fight. Which reply and which pronoun?
questions.answer: «Я вас не понял» (ya vas ne PO-nyal), 'I did not catch you', with вы creating distance, followed by stepping away.
questions.distractor: «Ты чего?» (ty chee-VO), 'what is with you?', because a question is always less aggressive than a statement.
questions.correction: The error is to assume that a question is automatically softer. ты чего is familiar, and its ты accepts the intimacy that the stranger has already claimed, which is exactly what you want to refuse; it works between peers and reads as a challenge from a stranger. The вы in я вас не понял refuses the frame, and the repair move forces him to repeat the words in front of whoever is present. T–V choice is part of the message rather than a decoration, which is the point the English Wikipedia article on the T–V distinction makes with its power and solidarity semantics. The exit is what turns the calm sentence into a boundary rather than a plea.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes de-escalation from submission, given that both may begin with a calm voice and no counter-insult?
questions.answer: The limit: de-escalation states it once and acts on it, so the behaviour stops or the exchange ends, while submission drops the limit and the behaviour continues.
questions.distractor: The volume: de-escalation is quiet and submission is apologetic.
questions.correction: The error is to look for a difference in tone rather than in outcome. Both can be quiet, and an apology can be either a boundary or a surrender depending on what follows it. The behavioural test is what you do after the sentence: «Я не буду это слушать» (ya ne BOO-doo EH-ta SLOO-shat'), 'I am not going to listen to this', is a limit because it can be carried out without the other person's consent, while «Ну ладно» (noo LAD-na), 'all right', accepts the continuation. Lesson 139 makes the distinction because learners often choose submission in the belief that it is de-escalation, and the result is that the behaviour they wanted to stop is reinforced.

questions.prompt: You must report a failed delivery to a client. Which version keeps the information and the urgency without the register?
questions.answer: «Поставка сорвалась, срок сдачи под угрозой» (pa-STAFF-ka sar-VA-las', SROK SDA-chee pat oog-RO-zoy), 'the delivery fell through and the deadline is at risk'.
questions.distractor: «Пипец, поставка сорвалась» (pee-PYETS, pa-STAFF-ka sar-VA-las'), because the euphemism is permitted and conveys the seriousness.
questions.correction: The error is to confuse permission with appropriateness. пипец is permitted in media with an age marking, and it is still a vulgar word in a client relationship, where the reader did not consent to the register and the message will be filed. The neutral version keeps both facts that matter, the failure and the risk to the deadline, and it adds authority rather than emotion. This is the production skill of lesson 140: a register rewrite must preserve the information and the urgency, and it fails if it also removes the pressure the reader needs to feel. What it removes is the speaker's state, not the situation's facts.

questions.prompt: In the capstone exchange, turn two is «Да блядь, я её вчера отправил» (da BLYAT', ya ye-YO fchee-RA at-PRA-veel). Turn three is «Не надо так со мной разговаривать» (nee NA-da tak sa MNOY raz-GA-va-ree-vat'). Which labels belong to each turn?
questions.answer: Turn two: target nobody, force expletive, register obscene in an institutional channel. Turn three: target the behaviour, force boundary, register professional.
questions.distractor: Turn two: target the hearer, force insult, register obscene. Turn three: force counter-insult, register hostile.
questions.correction: The error is to read turn two as an attack and turn three as a counter-attack. Turn two's obscenity is comma-separated and removable, so its target is nobody and its force is an expletive; the problem it creates is the channel rather than the hearer. Turn three names the behaviour rather than the person, uses no obscenity, and can be quoted without embarrassment, so its force is a boundary and its register is professional. Labelling correctly matters because the responses differ: an expletive in the wrong channel calls for a channel correction, while an insult calls for the repertoire in lesson 139. Reading both as aggression produces a conflict where there was a misjudgement.
